scope: Posthoc descriptor of caller-supplied geometry and samples; no producer authenticity, physical path identity, endpoint ownership, calibrated confidence or acceptance
summary: Accepted bounded descriptor and native receipt adapter. Seven supplied tests and 93 independent assertions pass; all 12 source blobs and the cited R103 review hash verify. Rigid rotation preserves lengths and signed turns. Reflection negates signed turns; reversed traversal reverses and negates the original turn sequence, apart from the documented ambiguous sign of an exact U-turn. Scaling points and corresponding full widths preserves dimensionless lengths. Zero-valued observed support remains observed with zero supported fraction; all-null support is UNKNOWN; eight malformed support cases reject. Missing/unilateral/degenerate edge pairs cannot establish centerline offsets. Actual W2 receipts recompute 27.75 and 64.75 px within floating-point tolerance and normalize to 0.75 and 1.75 configured corridor widths. This denominator is not calibrated hallway width. Native unknown remains unknown, despite all retained vertex samples exceeding threshold. Caller-supplied metadata remains a trust boundary: the adapter echoes reported counts/source claims separately from recomputed geometry, while countTurns trusts supplied descriptor rows. No acceptance laundering was found under the declared contract.

signedTurnTransform.reflection: signedRadians negated because the determinant changes sign while dot products are preserved
signedTurnTransform.reversedPath: new turn at each corresponding vertex is negative of the old turn, visited in reverse order; reverse widths with their segments
signedTurnTransform.screenFrame: The named canonical frame has y increasing down, so positive cross-product turns appear clockwise on screen.
signedTurnTransform.exactUTurn: Absolute angle pi is meaningful; sign may depend on signed zero/roundoff and is not asserted.
